title: Charles Hémard de Denonville, cardinal de Mâcon, Rome and Orvieto to Anne de Montmorency, 1536-37 (BnF fr. 3053; DECODE R4233-R4248)

steps.what: Checked Tomokiyo's francis.htm, Lasry's GL.htm, DECODE's sixteen fr. 3053 records and the Dodieu edition table for a published decipherment
Identified the catalogue's 'unknown sender' as the cardinal de Mâcon from Tomokiyo's description of the volume and from the clear signatures on R4239, R4240 and R4247
Fetched the sixteen record pages and the images of the eight target records from DECODE with the stored cookie
Applied 'Mascon's cipher' (macon_key.md, built in gramont1529 from Lasry's and Tomokiyo's tables) to the cipher lines
Glyph-level transcription of the cipher passages of all eight records by reading agents, one or two records at a time
Six contemporary marginal or interlinear decipherments found in the volume; three agree with the independent decoding word for word
Corrected the working table from a glossed line ('quant au faict de florence'): the big curly X is Q/U, not N, and the QUE group is written three ways
Read R4240 (~85%), R4247 letter 1 (~80%), R4238 (~65%), R4233 (~60%), passages of R4235 and R4239, and 66 lines of R4234
Found that the f. 85 cipher (R4248) is not Mâcon's but a second fr. 3053 cipher, deciphered in clear at the time on f. 86, and read the passage from that
Third pass, two reading agents at a time: R4234 P8-P12 (~58 lines) and P16-P20 (~30 lines, P15 a clear copy of P16 used as crib), with the corrected glyph values
Fetched DECODE's un-downloaded full-page views of R4234 (P4, P7, P10, P13, P14, P18) to check for a missing page: all duplicate the crops
R4235 P2-P3 (29 lines, ~80%) and passage D on P8 aligned with the contemporary clear copy on P6 (~92%); R4247 letter 2 (27 lines, ~75%, last six in fragments)
R4239 P3-P15, the 100 unread lines (~72%), with the clear text of P18-P22 as a running crib
Opened the eight sibling DECODE records R4236-R4246 via the API: all status Decrypted with no plaintext file attached; outside catalogue 180, not read

gaps.detail: barred-cross family reads F/P/O/U/V/D/H/S within a line, separable only by context; no gloss covers these groups
faded foot of P14; only fragments legible on the DECODE crop

gaps.item: proper names (Cesane, Palmier, Ambroise's surname, the Sienese gentleman)
gaps.detail: spelled in cipher but the letters do not settle to a known name

outcome.fraction_read_source: Not measurable token-wise (per-passage prose readings with per-letter percentages). Line-weighted after the third pass: ~445 of ~600 cipher lines (R4233 70x0.6, R4234 155x0.75, R4235 60x0.8, R4238 26x0.65, R4239 160x0.72, R4240 26x0.85, R4247 57x0.8 + 27x0.6, R4248 20 via f. 86). R4234's earlier ~250-line estimate was high: ~155 on the crops.
outcome.notes: Seven records read in part, one (R4248) resolved by the contemporary decipherment on the next leaf. The limit is the hand and the ambiguous barred-cross signs, not the cryptanalysis: the key was known before the attempt. Third pass (21 Sept 2026) deciphered every remaining page; the residue is the barred-cross signs, a faded foot and names. Key recovered (Tomokiyo/Lasry Mascon's cipher, corrected from glosses; R4248's second table given by f. 86); codes_open counts only the unexplained ·52 of R4239 P30, total not counted.

prior.where: Contemporary marginal and interlinear decipherments of some passages in the volume itself, and a full clear decipherment of the f. 85 cipher on f. 86. No printed or online plaintext: Tomokiyo and Lasry publish the key only.

human: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images
